content.title: Really related to CNNs?
content.review:
This paper presented the study on complex kernel for shape detection, which is inspired by quantum theory. This paper started from the description of the shape detection problem, then introduced the traditional Bayesian and Hough transform approaches. In Section 4, the proposed quantum inspired complex kernel was described.

Overall I like the study on complex kernel and expect deeper study and real application to convolutional neural networks. At this stage, I cannot recommend "accept", but it would be accepted if the study of the application to CNNs is conducted.

content.title: The paper presents an interesting, but very preliminary idea, to use quantum inspired complex kernels that can be potentially used inside CNNs.
content.rating: 4: Ok but not good enough - rejection
content.review:
Abstract: The paper presents an interesting, but very preliminary idea, to use quantum inspired complex kernels that can be potentially used inside CNNs.

Format review: The paper is well written in general, has clear language and explanations. The figures and tables are well formatted and are visually appealing.

Method review: It is very hard to assess the validity of the method for anyone not familiar with the quantum physics field. The proposal seems sound, but it is also not complete, as the title of the paper suggests.

Experiments review: The experiment is too limited to derive any meaningful conclusions. Even with the extensions (experiments with noisy data) the authors offer, the problem proposed is too simple to demonstrate that the method is really useful.

Conclusion: It is a very interesting idea that should be further developed and tested. The paper is possibly the tip of an iceberg in a novel, promising field. However, the validity of the method is hard to assess theoretically and the experiments are very weak to prove anything.

content.title: This submission's quality is clearly lower than that of ICLR papers
content.review:
This submission develops a deep method by using complex-valued kernel functions in Convolutional Neural Networks. The global idea can be interesting to a part of the community. However, the submission has issues in the following main aspects:

1. Regarding the validation of the idea/method, only circle detection is considered in the submission. This is not enough, in particular considering the fact the circle is one most regular 2D shape.

2. Regarding the writing quality, there are a large number of expression/language issues in the submission. For instance, there already exhibit quite a few obvious problems in the abstract. To name a few:
        - Convolution Neural Networks
        - Understanding the role of these layers, …, are all ongoing research questions.
        - Complex value kernel functions
        - is robustness to

Also, the formatting of the citations within the text (in particular in the case where the authors or the publication are not included in the sentence) does not follow the formatting Instructions for ICLR2018.

3. It lacks a necessary review of related works. In total, only 12 papers are cited, in which only 5 are published after 2000.

content.title: About review of related work and research
content.comment:
Dear Reviewer 1,

thank you for your attention. A question: you claim it lacks a necessary review of related work. Can you point to us what you mean ? we did a review, but of course, we can't claim to have reviewed every work it exists. So if you have pointers to what you think is related work, preferably more than one pointer, we are very interested to learn. 

On the issue of validating our work with experiments on a circle, you may have used your "culture of research" to say "it is not enough", but we disagree. This paper is not using the same ideas of others and improving it by a percent. This is a new idea with a new  theoretical basis that could perhaps make an impact in the future (the title may not be appropriate, as we meant "towards" to mean, hopefully the direction will get there.  We demonstrated on a simple shape, but we demonstrated since we compared to the "classical " techniques and the theory explained it.  It is novel!! This is what some "research cultures" value, new ideas and demonstration of the idea and consider enough to open a field.  So why is  not enough ? what is the rational ? 

In summary, we would appreciate if instead of just categorically  saying "no", you provided concrete feedback.

content.title: Perhaps you can reconsider
content.comment:
Dear Review 2,
thank you for your effort and review. We appreciated your candid remarks and gives us a clear  understanding of the limitations.  We will try to answer some of the points you made and try to plant a seed on your mind to reconsider your "scores". 
Yes, there are clear references to physics literature and not everyone is familiar. But note that the paper is self contained technically, i.e., all derivations are justified in the paper. The only assumption from physics was the use of a particular Kernel (complex valued one with the optimization criteria in the exponent) and to use it by summing over all paths (we approximated by an empirical sum over the data). So other than that, there is no use of quantum physics.  If you understood the steps, you understood everything (other than the assumption). 
On the issue of validating our work with simple experiments  we think  this  is a new idea with a new  theoretical basis that could perhaps make an impact in the future (the title may not be appropriate, as we meant "towards" to mean, hopefully the direction will get there but most likely we would have to change to "quantum kernels").  Also the experiments were meant to be illustration of the theory. So we see the experiments as a demonstration of the theory on a simple shape, but we demonstrated since we compared to the "classical " techniques and the theory explained it.  It is novel!! This is what some "research cultures" value, new ideas and demonstration of the idea and consider enough to open a field.  We would have thought that if you  appreciate the novelty (and not be distracted by the use of the word quantum) that would put the score up.   But in any case, thank you for your candid review.

content.title: Quantum Kernels
content.comment:
Dear Review 3,

indeed we barely connected to the CNN. A much better title, in retrospect, to reflect the work would be "Quantum Kernels", since this is really what we proposed. We just thought that if we are proposing "Quantum Kernels"  it is natural to think that it may lead to Quantum CNN, so we use the word "towards" in this sense. But again, Quantum Kernels would be the final title if accepted (and if not, we will submit elsewhere with the new title). 
thanks

But why reject a new idea that is clearly of interest by this community ? we thought we demonstrated well, in theory and the experiments demonstrate it can be applied.  Isn't this of interest ? why reject ?

thanks anyway for the feedback
